title: Tracking Misinformation: Delhi Protest Photo Claims
summary: Online commentators have suggested that this image from our October 2026 Delhi protest coverage was taken in 2020. This is false; the image was taken by Saumya Khandelwal on October 10 alongside…
body_markdown:
Claims circulating online falsely suggest this image from our October 2026 Delhi protest coverage was taken in 2020.


Online commentators have suggested that this image from our October 2026 Delhi protest coverage was taken in 2020. This is false; the image was taken by Saumya Khandelwal on October 10 alongside dozens of other[images and video](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/10/09/world/india-cjp-cockroach-protest) from that day. The image also appeared on our[Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/DeUz4uqAHdo/?hl=en&img_index=4) as part of a photo carousel.


The New York Times has had multiple photographers on the ground in New Delhi this month, covering the[protests](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/09/world/asia/what-to-know-about-the-delhi-protests.html) , the scores of[young Indians](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/10/world/asia/police-india-cockroach-protest-anger.html) who have arrived in Delhi to protest the erasure of millions of people from voter rolls, and the wider[youth movement](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/07/24/world/asia/india-protest-cockroach-party-timeline.html) . This includes Saumya, a talented photographer who took this defining image of the protests and has worked with the Times for the past eight years.


Readers can follow the latest reporting, photography and video from the protests[here](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/12/world/asia/india-protests-congress-rahul-gandhi.html) .
